title: Temporal Drift Failure Atlas and Remediation Hypotheses
content:
Status: DRAFT - working notes for triage meeting.

Summary:
This is an investigative log for a class of onboarding regressions that show clear temporal structure: model responses degrade (in quality metrics and a handful of user-facing signal checks) along weekday/weekend and hourly patterns after a model version bump plus traffic shift on 2025-09-18. The goal is to decompose the failure surface across time, prompt archetype, and routing behavior so we can propose quick mitigations and medium-term fixes.

Key takeaways (quick):
- Regression onset aligns with two events: v2.3 promotion to production (2025-09-18) and a changeset that altered sampling temperature heuristics for short prompts.
- Error incidence is ~3.2% -> 7.9% (relative to baseline precision metric) for a monitored prompt subset, but the increase is concentrated in 03:00–07:00 UTC and high-load bursts (observed in Dedicated early-morning batch jobs).
- Prompt archetypes affected: short instruction-only prompts (<20 tokens), multi-turn followups without explicit system context, and some time-sensitive news queries.
- Hypotheses split between model-behavior drift (temperature scheduling + quantization interactions) and routing-induced model mismatch (requests sent to lower-capacity variant during autoscale).

Scope and constraints:
- This document covers production onboarding evals (seeded promptset) and live traffic signals for customer beta cluster "beta-west-1". Not covering embeddings or reranking use-cases here.
- We only examine promptset slices used in onboarding tests + the 2k sample corpus used by QA.

Eval setup and data sources used:
- Onboarding eval harness: onboarding_v3/promptset_A (2,001 prompts, 8 archetypes), runs daily against curated model snapshot and two fallback variants.
- Telemetry: per-request latency/cost, model_variant, server_id, UTC timestamp, token_stats, and human-rated quality (post-deployment A/B QA).
- Time window analyzed: 2025-09-01 -> 2025-10-15 (captures pre/post promotion).

Observed patterns (high-level):
1) Temporal spikes: Two prominent spikes in failure rate recurring daily ~03:00–07:00 UTC. Correlates with autoscale events where requests were routed to model-variant X-small (quantized) for short bursts.
2) Prompt-length sensitivity: Short instruction prompts saw hallucination/omission errors increase 3x. Longer prompts stable.
3) Context-drop in multi-turn: When previous messages are <40 tokens and KV-cache warmed colder due to routing across heterogeneous nodes, coherence drops.
4) News/time queries: A subset of time-sensitive prompts degrade selectively, likely due to a knowledge cutoff mismatch between variants.

Temporal decomposition (notes):
- Buckets: local-peak (03–07 UTC), off-peak (08–16 UTC), regional-peak (17–22 UTC).
- For each bucket we computed: precision@K for reference answers; token-efficiency delta; and human disagreement score.
- Result: local-peak has worst precision and highest variance in token-efficiency -> suggests non-deterministic behavior from variant mix.

Failure archetypes (examples):
A. Abrupt omission: model returns empty/placeholder or a generic "I don't know" for direct instructions (e.g., "Summarize this page in 3 bullets").
B. Hallucinatory filler: invented facts for short prompts that should have relied on prompt-only context.
C. Decontextualized followup: multi-turn answers ignore previous message nuance, producing contradictory statements.
D. Stale-reference answers: answers referencing knowledge past the variant's cutoff date (e.g., saying an event occurred before it did).

Representative prompts (anonymized):
- "List the top 3 benefits of enabling X in config Y" (short instruction)
- "Followup: Why is it slower?" (multi-turn without system restatement)
- "Who won the 2025 Pacific cup?" (time-sensitive)

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
H1 - Variant-mix routing: autoscaler intermittently routes to a quantized small-variant that has subtle decoding differences (temperature / sampling seeds). Evidence: model_variant field spikes align with failure spikes.
H2 - Temperature scheduling change: recent change to lower temperature for prompts <20 tokens introduced a bifurcation in output probability mass for short queries.
H3 - KV-cache warming: frequent cross-node routing evicts warmed caches, harming multi-turn coherency.
H4 - Evaluation set leakage: onboarding seed prompts underrepresent early-morning batch jobs; hence baseline missed this regime. (less likely but actionable)
H5 - Data drift: incoming user prompts changed formulation in the evening/regional time windows; partially supported by lexical shifts in telemetry.

Quick/low-risk mitigations (can ship within 48–72h):
- Pin routing policy for onboarding evals and beta-west-1 traffic to avoid X-small variant until we validate parity (config change, rollback autoscale preference). (owner: Tom)
- Revert the temperature change for short prompts in the runtime default; instead gate it behind an opt-in flag while we run AB tests. (owner: Miguel)
- Add a short-term heuristic: for multi-turn sequences shorter than 40 tokens, prefer same-server sticky routing for next request (reduces KV eviction). (owner: SRE/Runtime)

Medium-term remediation (2–6 weeks):
- Re-run thorough calibration of quantized variant on the short-prompt subset; produce a small calibration table mapping prompt-length -> decoding config. (owner: applied-ml)
- Expand onboarding eval harness to include time-of-day stratification and artificially injected autoscale routing cases (simulate variant-mix). (owner: QA/Applied-ML)
- Implement deterministic seeding for sampling in the quantized variant when request originates from onboarding test pipeline (so we can compare apples-to-apples). (owner: serving-runtime)

Experiments to run (priority order):
1) Shadow run: route 100% of onboarding eval traffic to quantized-small in a shadow experiment (no customer impact) to reproduce failure distribution. Measure per-archetype deltas.
2) Temperature sweep AB: for short prompts, sweep temperature [0.0, 0.2, 0.4] across matched seeds on both full and quantized variants.
3) Sticky-routing A/B: test sticky-routing for 50% of multi-turn short sessions. Evaluate coherence, latency impact, and server load.

Monitoring and SLOs to add:
- Add an "archetype-precision" time-series for short-instruction archetype and threshold alert if delta > 2% absolute compared to baseline over 1h window.
- Add variant-distribution dashboard: per-minute breakdown of model_variant for key routes.
- Add human disagreement sampling targeted at 03:00–07:00 UTC to catch regressions fast.

Decision log (proposed):
- Immediate: Pin beta-west-1 routing away from X-small (decision window: 24 hours).
- Short: Revert temp short-prompt change and enable AB runs (48–72 hours).
- Medium: Run calibration + expand harness (2–6 weeks).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there de-serialization or tokenizer differences between variants that only appear for very short sequences? Need a token-level diff tool.
- Could the autoscaler be collapsing requests by mistake (i.e., merging user contexts)? Logs show no obvious merges, but deeper trace is needed.
- Is the human QA batch that reported this biased toward the UTC window? (check QA sampling policy)

Action items (owners):
- Tom: Pin routing for beta-west-1, validate with shadow traffic (ETA: 24h).
- Miguel: Revert temperature change or gate behind feature flag + start sweep AB (ETA: 48h).
- Caroline/Rina: Add time-of-day slices to onboarding harness and schedule nightly runs across all variants (ETA: 1 week).
- SRE: Implement sticky routing experiment for multi-turn sessions (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Applied-ML: Run quantized variant calibration and produce config table (ETA: 3 weeks).

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- If H1 proven true, we should prioritize variant parity tests in the onboarding checklist before any model promotion.
- Keep customer impact comms minimal but transparent: internal incident note + short blurb for affected beta customers.
- Save failing examples daily to gs://redwood-alerts/temporal-failures/<date>.json for easy review at standups.

Next meeting: 2025-11-12 09:00 UTC - triage with SRE, Runtime, and QA.

Appendix (quick artifacts):
- Link to time-series plots: confluence:ML-Onboarding/temporal-graphs
- Notebook with decomposition: gs://redwood-experiments/temporal-decomp.ipynb
- Quick checklist for rolling back temp change in runtime: github:github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/67

End of doc (draft).
